text: dsh-superagent 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 GitHub 编码代理，也可接入飞书消息。它将获准的 Issue、PR 或评论交给评估与策略流程，再为每张工单创建独立的 DSH 执行会话和工作目录。系统提供 GitHub 事件接收、工单执行、状态管理面板、任务结果回传及可选飞书来源，适合希望让团队编码代理持续处理仓库任务的维护者。需要配置有仓库写权限的 GitHub 账号、gh 与 git；飞书接入另需机器人和 lark-cli。

dsh-superagent routes authorized GitHub issues and comments to dedicated DSH worker sessions and workspaces. It evaluates requests by policy, executes accepted tickets, and shows status in a web panel. Configure a writable GitHub account, gh and git; optional Feishu support needs a bot and lark-cli.
想让编码代理根据 GitHub Issue 自动开始处理任务。
能不能把 PR 评论交给 DSH 里的独立会话完成？
希望限制哪些 GitHub 账号可以给仓库代理派活。
让代理在做完代码后直接回复原来的讨论并开 PR。
我想在飞书里给仓库编码代理发任务。
有没有带面板的工具可以查看待处理的代理工单？
I want GitHub issues routed to a coding agent with a separate workspace.
Can a DSH agent pick up authorized pull request comments and report back?
dsh-superagent 的功能「GitHub 工单接收」：监听仓库 Issue、PR 与讨论评论，将事件整理为供策略评估的触发项。 通过配置的来源触发。
dsh-superagent 的功能「独立会话执行」：接受的工单拥有持久 DSH worker 会话和各自工作目录，执行过程与其他工单分开。 通过配置的来源触发。
dsh-superagent 的功能「策略评估与授权」：评估候选请求并依据策略决定是否接收，未获允许的账号不能发起工作。 通过配置的来源触发。
dsh-superagent 的功能「Web 管理面板」：在 DSH Web 中提供 Superagent 管理界面，展示工单和运行状态以便人工跟进。 通过配置的来源触发。
dsh-superagent 的功能「可选飞书消息来源」：通过可配置的 Feishu Source 接收消息并把消息转换为工单触发项。 通过配置的来源触发。

dsh-superagent README · dsh-superagent：This repository is a fork of [deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype). It keeps the upstream design and adds the changes under [Fork notes](#fork-notes--本分支说明).

dsh-superagent README · dsh-superagent：dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

dsh-superagent README · dsh-superagent：It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.
dsh-superagent README · Install：dsh-superagent is a DSH bundle: `dsh plugin` installs it into one profile, next to the plugins that profile already loads.

dsh-superagent README · Requirements：- [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/) 0.2.1-alpha.2 or later. The desktop app 0.2.1-rc.5 is known to work.
- `gh` 2.48 or later and `git` 2.32 or later on `PATH`: the GitHub Source calls `gh`, and ticket checkouts use `git`.
- Optional, only for the Feishu Source: `lark-cli` and a Feishu or Lark app with a bot.

Node.js 22.19+ or 24+ is needed only when you build from source; the release tarball ships the built `lib/`.

dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-superagent
```

dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-superagent-<version>.tgz
```

dsh-superagent README · Restart and open the panel：Restart that profile — quit and reopen the desktop app, or restart `dsh web` — then choose **Superagent** in the sidebar.

The bundle ships a default state directory, `<DSH_HOME>/state/dsh-superagent`, for its database, locks, worker shims and ticket directories. To keep it elsewhere, add this to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` before the first start:

```yaml
- id: dsh-superagent
  config:
    stateDir: /absolute/path
```

`stateDir` cannot change after the first start.

dsh-superagent README · Configure it：1. **Sources → GitHub**: the repository as `owner/name`, and the `gh` CLI the agent acts as. The agent comments, pushes and opens pull requests as that account, so it needs write access; a dedicated account keeps its work distinguishable from yours.
2. **Policy**: the GitHub logins allowed to ask for work. Until the list has someone, no request can become a ticket.
3. **Execution**: the ticket directory root and a `prepare` command that gives each ticket its own checkout, for example a `git worktree` of a local clone.

dsh-superagent README · Configure it：Then ask for work from an allowed account: open an Issue or comment on one, mentioning the agent, for example `@<agent-login> fix the typo in the README`. With [shared-account mode](#shared-account-mode), the comment must *start* with the mention.

[docs/006-deployment.md](docs/006-deployment.md) covers the accounts, the `prepare` command template, upgrades and troubleshooting; [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is the guided setup an agent can follow with you.

dsh-superagent README · Setup：Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

dsh-superagent README · Fork notes / 本分支说明：This copy adds two changes on top of the upstream research prototype, for using it inside a shared DSH profile with one GitHub account:

dsh-superagent README · Fork notes / 本分支说明：- **One account can request and act.** A message the agent's own account writes counts as that account's explicit request when it *starts* with `@<login>`; its other messages (acknowledgements, progress, results) are still ignored, so the agent cannot trigger itself in a loop.
- **The worker environment stays out of the host process.** `PATH`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` are applied only for the setup check and restored at once. Installing the bundle into a profile you also use for other Sessions no longer changes their git or `PATH`; worker sessions use the operator's own CLI and git configuration, which one shared account makes equivalent.

dsh-superagent README · Shared-account mode：When the agent and the people asking share one GitHub account, mentioning yourself sends no notification, so the Source cannot rely on the account's notifications. Turn on **Receive new Issues** and **Receive comments in the repository** on the GitHub Source; it then reads the repository directly, and a comment that starts with the agent's mention becomes an explicit request. Messages of that account that do not start with the mention are treated as the agent's own output and ignored, which keeps acknowledgements and results from triggering new tickets.
